title.en: Volume 52 Book of Later Tang 28: Biographies 4 - Li Sizhao, Pei Yue, Li Siben, Li Si'en
title.raw: 卷五十二 唐書28: 列傳四 李嗣昭 裴約 李嗣本 李嗣恩 Volume 52 Book of Later Tang 28: Biographies 4 - Li Sizhao, Pei Yue, Li Siben, Li Si'en

sentences.zh: 李嗣昭，字益光，武皇母弟代州刺史克柔之假子也。

translations.literal: Li Sizhao, courtesy name Yiguang, was the adopted son of Kerou, military commissioner of Dai and younger brother of the Martial Emperor's mother.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao, whose courtesy name was Yiguang, was the adopted son of Kerou, military commissioner of Dai and younger brother of the Martial Emperor's mother.

sentences.zh: 小字進通，不知族姓所出。

translations.literal: His childhood name was Jintong; his clan and surname of origin are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: He was also known in youth as Jintong, but his original clan and surname are unknown.

sentences.zh: （《歐陽史》作本姓韓氏，汾州大穀縣民家子。）〉

translations.literal: (The Ouyang History states that his original surname was Han and that he was the son of a common household in Dagu County, Fen Prefecture.)]
translations.idiomatic: (The Ouyang History records that he was originally surnamed Han and came from a common family in Dagu County, Fen Prefecture.)]

sentences.zh: 少事克柔，頗謹願，雖形貌眇小，而精悍有膽略，沉毅不群。

translations.literal: In youth he served Kerou and was quite dutiful and compliant; though small in stature, he was keen and bold in spirit, deep and resolute, and unlike others.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he served Kerou with dutiful steadiness. Though slight in build, he was sharp, courageous, and unusually composed.

sentences.zh: 初嗜酒好樂，武皇微伸儆戒，乃終身不飲。

translations.literal: At first he loved wine and music; the Martial Emperor gave him a mild warning, and thereafter he never drank for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: He had once been fond of wine and music, but after the Martial Emperor gently admonished him, he never drank again for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 少從征伐，精練軍機。

translations.literal: From youth he followed campaigns and became thoroughly versed in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He took the field from an early age and became thoroughly skilled in military operations.

sentences.zh: 乾寧初，王珂、王珙爭帥河中，珙引陝州之軍攻珂，珂求救於武皇，乃令嗣昭將兵援之，敗珙軍於猗氏，獲賊將李璠等。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianning, Wang Ke and Wang Gong contended for command of Hezhong; Gong brought troops from Shaan Prefecture to attack Ke. Ke sought rescue from the Martial Emperor, who then ordered Sizhao to lead troops to aid him. He defeated Gong's army at Yishi and captured the rebel generals Li Fan and others.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianning era, Wang Ke and Wang Gong fought over command of Hezhong. Gong brought Shaan troops against Ke, who appealed to the Martial Emperor. Sizhao was sent to his aid, defeated Gong at Yishi, and captured the rebel general Li Fan and others.

sentences.zh: 四年，改衙內都將，復援河中，敗汴軍於胡壁堡，擒汴將滑禮，以功加檢校僕射。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was changed to commander-in-chief of the inner guard, again aided Hezhong, defeated Bian troops at Hubi Fort, captured the Bian general Hua Li, and for his merit was promoted to acting Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made commander of the inner guard, returned to aid Hezhong, routed Bian forces at Hubi Fort, captured the Bian general Hua Li, and was promoted to acting Grand Mentor for his service.

sentences.zh: 及王珂請婚武皇，武皇以女妻之；

translations.literal: When Wang Ke requested marriage with the Martial Emperor, the Martial Emperor gave him his daughter as wife;
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Ke sought a marriage alliance with the Martial Emperor, the latter gave him his daughter in marriage;

sentences.zh: 珂赴禮於太原，以嗣昭權典河中留後事。

translations.literal: Ke went to Taiyuan for the wedding rites, and Sizhao was appointed to administer the acting military governorship of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Ke traveled to Taiyuan for the wedding, and Sizhao was left in charge of Hezhong as acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 李罕之襲我潞州也，嗣昭率師攻潞州，與汴將丁會戰於含口，俘獲三千，執其將蔡延恭；

translations.literal: When Li Hanzhi attacked our Luzhou, Sizhao led troops to assault Luzhou and fought the Bian general Ding Hui at Hankou, capturing three thousand and seizing his general Cai Yangong;
translations.idiomatic: When Li Hanzhi seized our Luzhou, Sizhao marched to retake it and fought the Bian general Ding Hui at Hankou, taking three thousand prisoners and capturing his general Cai Yangong;

sentences.zh: 代李君慶為蕃漢馬步行營都將，進攻潞州，遣李存質、李嗣本以兵扼天井關。

translations.literal: He replaced Li Junqing as commander of the mixed Tangut-Han horse and foot field army, advanced on Luzhou, and sent Li Cunzhi and Li Siben with troops to block Tianjing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Replacing Li Junqing as commander of the mixed Tangut-Han field army, he pressed the attack on Luzhou and sent Li Cunzhi and Li Siben to hold Tianjing Pass.

sentences.zh: 汴將澤州刺史劉屺棄城而遁，乃以李存璋為刺史。

translations.literal: The Bian general Liu Qi, prefect of Ze Prefecture, abandoned the city and fled, whereupon Li Cunzhang was appointed prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian prefect of Ze, Liu Qi, abandoned his city and fled, and Li Cunzhang was installed as the new prefect.

sentences.zh: 梁祖聞嗣昭之師大至，召葛從周謂曰：「並人若在高平，當圍而取之，先須野戰，勿以潞州為敵。

translations.literal: When the Liang founder heard that Sizhao's army had arrived in force, he summoned Ge Congzhou and said, "If the Bing men are at Gaoping, they should be surrounded and taken; first engage them in the field—do not make Luzhou the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Sizhao's army was approaching in strength, the Liang founder summoned Ge Congzhou and said, "If the Bing troops are at Gaoping, surround and take them. Fight them in the open first—do not fix your attention on Luzhou alone."

sentences.zh: 」及聞嗣昭軍韓店，梁祖曰：「進通扼八議路，此賊決與我鬥，公等臨事製機，勿落奸便。

translations.literal: "When he heard that Sizhao's army was at Handian, the Liang founder said, "Jintong is blocking the Bayi Road—this bandit is determined to fight us. You must adapt to circumstances as events unfold and not fall for his tricks."
translations.idiomatic: "Learning that Sizhao's army was at Handian, the Liang founder said, "Jintong has blocked the Bayi Road—this enemy means to give battle. Adapt to events on the spot and do not let him lure you into a trap."

sentences.zh: 」賀德倫閉壁不出，嗣昭日以鐵騎環城，汴人不敢芻牧，援路斷絕。

translations.literal: He Delun shut the walls and would not come out; day after day Sizhao sent iron cavalry to circle the city, and the Bian men dared not pasture or forage; their supply routes were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: He Delun held the walls and refused to come out. Sizhao sent armored cavalry to ring the city day after day, so the Bian troops could not graze or forage and their lines of supply were severed.

sentences.zh: 八月，德倫、張歸厚棄城遁去，我復取潞州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month He Delun and Zhang Guihou abandoned the city and fled; we recovered Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month He Delun and Zhang Guihou abandoned the city and fled, and we retook Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 光化三年，汴人攻滄州，劉仁恭求救，遣嗣昭出師邢、洺以應之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guanghua the Bian attacked Cangzhou; Liu Rengong sought rescue, and Sizhao was dispatched with an army through Xing and Mo to respond.
translations.idiomatic: In Guanghua 3 the Bian attacked Cangzhou. Liu Rengong appealed for help, and Sizhao was sent through Xing and Mo to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭遇汴軍於沙河，擊敗之，獲其將胡禮。

translations.literal: Sizhao encountered Bian troops at Shahe, defeated them, and captured their general Hu Li.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao met the Bian army at Shahe, routed it, and captured their general Hu Li.

sentences.zh: 進攻洺州，下之，獲其郡將朱紹宗。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Mo Prefecture, took it, and captured its prefectural commander Zhu Shaozong.
translations.idiomatic: He then attacked and captured Mo Prefecture, taking its commander Zhu Shaozong prisoner.

sentences.zh: 九月，梁祖自率軍三萬至臨洺，葛從周設伏於青山口。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Liang founder personally led thirty thousand troops to Linmo, and Ge Congzhou set an ambush at Qingshan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Liang founder led thirty thousand men in person to Linmo, while Ge Congzhou laid an ambush at Qingshan Pass.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭聞梁祖至，斂軍而退，從周伏兵發，為其所敗，偏將王郃郎、楊師悅等被擒。

translations.literal: When Sizhao heard that the Liang founder had arrived, he drew in his army and withdrew; Congzhou's ambush struck, and Sizhao was defeated by them; the subordinate generals Wang Helang, Yang Shiyue, and others were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the Liang founder's arrival, Sizhao drew back his forces, only to be caught by Congzhou's ambush. Subordinate generals including Wang Helang and Yang Shiyue were taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 十月，汴人大寇鎮、定，王郜告急於武皇，乃遣嗣昭出師，下太行，擊懷、孟。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Bian made a great raid on Zhen and Ding; Wang Gao reported urgently to the Martial Emperor, who then dispatched Sizhao with an army down the Taihang Mountains to strike Huai and Meng.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Bian launched a major assault on Zhen and Ding. Wang Gao sent an urgent appeal to the Martial Emperor, who dispatched Sizhao down the Taihang to strike Huai and Meng.

sentences.zh: 汴將侯信守河陽，不意嗣昭之師至，既無守備，驅市人登城；

translations.literal: The Bian general Hou Xin held Heyang and did not expect Sizhao's army to arrive; having no preparations for defense, he drove townspeople onto the walls;
translations.idiomatic: The Bian general Hou Xin held Heyang and was caught unprepared by Sizhao's arrival. With no real defenses ready, he pressed townspeople onto the walls;

sentences.zh: 嗣昭攻其北門，破其外垣，俄而汴將閻寶救軍至，乃退。

translations.literal: Sizhao attacked the north gate and breached the outer wall; presently the Bian general Yan Bao's relief army arrived, and he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao assaulted the north gate and broke through the outer wall, but when the Bian general Yan Bao's relief force arrived shortly afterward, he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，嗣昭進兵蒲縣。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year Sizhao advanced his army to Pu County.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the first month, Sizhao advanced to Pu County.

sentences.zh: 十八日，汴將朱友寧、氏叔琮將兵十萬來拒。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day the Bian generals Zhu Youning and Shi Shuzong led one hundred thousand troops to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth the Bian generals Zhu Youning and Shi Shuzong arrived with one hundred thousand men to block him.

sentences.zh: 二十八日，梁祖自率大軍至平陽，嗣昭之師大恐。

translations.literal: On the twenty-eighth day the Liang founder personally led a great army to Pingyang, and Sizhao's troops were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-eighth the Liang founder brought his main army to Pingyang in person, and Sizhao's forces were thrown into great fear.

sentences.zh: 三月十一日，有白虹貫周德威之營，候者雲不利，宜班師。

translations.literal: On the eleventh day of the third month a white rainbow pierced Zhou Dewei's camp; observers said it was inauspicious and that the army should withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh of the third month a white rainbow spanned Zhou Dewei's camp. Observers called it an ill omen and urged a withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 翌日，氏叔琮犯德威之營，汴軍十餘萬列陣四合，德威、嗣昭血戰解之，乃保軍而退，汴軍因乘之。

translations.literal: The next day Shi Shuzong assaulted Dewei's camp; more than one hundred thousand Bian troops formed battle lines on all four sides. Dewei and Sizhao fought bloody battles to break free, then protected the army in retreat, and the Bian troops pressed the advantage.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Shi Shuzong attacked Dewei's camp. More than one hundred thousand Bian troops closed in from every side. Dewei and Sizhao fought their way out in a bloody engagement and covered the army's retreat, but the Bian pressed hard in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 時諸將潰散，無復部伍，德威引騎軍循西山而遁，朱友寧乘勝陷慈、隰、汾等州。

translations.literal: At that time the generals scattered in rout and no longer kept formation; Dewei led the cavalry along the western mountains in flight, and Zhu Youning pressed the victory to seize Ci, Xi, Fen, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The generals broke and scattered, their formations lost. Dewei led the cavalry along the western hills in flight, while Zhu Youning pressed the victory and seized Ci, Xi, Fen, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 武皇聞其敗也，遣李存信率牙兵至清源應接，復為汴軍所擊。

translations.literal: When the Martial Emperor heard of the defeat, he sent Li Cunxin leading the guard troops to Qingyuan to link up, but they were again struck by Bian troops.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the defeat, the Martial Emperor sent Li Cunxin with the guard troops to Qingyuan to reinforce them, but they too were struck by the Bian army.

sentences.zh: 汴軍營於晉祠，嗣昭、德威收合餘眾，登城拒守；

translations.literal: The Bian army encamped at Jinci; Sizhao and Dewei gathered the remaining troops, mounted the walls, and held in defense;
translations.idiomatic: The Bian encamped at Jinci. Sizhao and Dewei rallied the survivors, manned the walls, and held the city;

sentences.zh: 汴人治攻具於西北隅，四面營柵相望。

translations.literal: the Bian men prepared siege engines at the northwest corner, and on all four sides their camp palisades faced one another.
translations.idiomatic: while the Bian prepared siege engines at the northwest corner and ringed the city with camps on every side.

sentences.zh: 時鎮州、河中皆為梁有，孤城無援，師旅敗亡。

translations.literal: At that time Zhen Prefecture and Hezhong were both held by Liang; the isolated city had no relief, and the army was broken and dying.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen and Hezhong were already in Liang hands. The city stood alone without relief, and the army was shattered.

sentences.zh: 武皇晝夜登城，憂不遑食，召諸將欲出保雲州，嗣昭曰：「王勿為此謀，兒等苟存，必能城守。

translations.literal: Day and night the Martial Emperor mounted the walls, too anxious to eat, and summoned the generals intending to go out and hold Yun Prefecture. Sizhao said, "Your Majesty, do not adopt this plan—as long as we sons remain alive, we can surely hold the city."
translations.idiomatic: Day and night the Martial Emperor walked the walls, too troubled to eat, and summoned his generals to discuss abandoning the city for Yun Prefecture. Sizhao said, "Your Majesty, do not consider that course. While we yet live, we can hold this city."

sentences.zh: 」李存信曰：「事勢危急，不如且入北蕃，別圖進取。

translations.literal: "Li Cunxin said, "The situation is critically urgent; better for now to enter the northern barbarians' lands and plan another advance later."
translations.idiomatic: "Li Cunxin said, "The situation is desperate. Better to withdraw into the northern tribes for now and seek another opening later."

sentences.zh: 朱溫兵師百萬，天下無敵，關東、河北受他指揮，今獨守危城，兵亡地蹙，儻彼築室反耕，環塹深固，則亡無日矣！

translations.literal: Zhu Wen's army numbers in the millions and is unmatched under heaven; east of the passes and Hebei all obey his command. Now we alone hold a perilous city, our troops lost and our territory compressed—if they build houses and turn to farming, with deep trenches and solid ramparts all around, then destruction will come in no time!"
translations.idiomatic: "Zhu Wen commands armies said to number in the millions and stands unmatched in the realm. East of the passes and in Hebei all obey him. We alone cling to a doomed city with our forces spent and our land shrinking. If they settle in for a long siege with deep trenches and strong ramparts, we are finished!"

sentences.zh: 」武皇將從之，嗣昭亟爭不可，猶豫未決，賴劉太妃極言於內，武後且止。

translations.literal: "The Martial Emperor was about to follow this advice; Sizhao urgently argued that it must not be done. Still undecided, he was saved when Grand Consort Liu spoke forcefully within, and the Martial Emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: "The Martial Emperor was on the point of agreeing. Sizhao argued urgently against it, and the emperor still hesitated until Grand Consort Liu spoke forcefully from within the palace, after which he set the plan aside.

sentences.zh: 數日，亡散之眾復集。

translations.literal: Within several days the scattered troops gathered again.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days the scattered troops rallied again.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭晝夜分兵四出，斬將搴旗，汴軍保守不暇。

translations.literal: Day and night Sizhao divided his troops to strike out on four sides, beheading generals and seizing banners; the Bian army had no leisure even to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night Sizhao sent detachments in every direction, killing enemy officers and capturing their banners, so the Bian could barely hold their own positions.

sentences.zh: 二十一日，朱友寧燒營退去，嗣昭追擊，復收汾、慈、隰等州。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day Zhu Youning burned his camp and withdrew; Sizhao pursued and recovered Fen, Ci, Xi, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first Zhu Youning burned his camp and withdrew. Sizhao pursued and recovered Fen, Ci, Xi, and the other lost prefectures.

sentences.zh: 五月，雲州都將王敬暉據城叛，振武石善友亦為部將契讓所逐，嗣昭皆討平之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Wang Jinghui, commander of Yun Prefecture, seized the city in rebellion; at Zhenwu, Shi Shanyou was also driven out by his subordinate general Qi Rang—Sizhao suppressed and pacified them both.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Wang Jinghui of Yun Prefecture rebelled and held the city, while at Zhenwu Shi Shanyou was driven out by his subordinate Qi Rang. Sizhao put down both rebellions.

sentences.zh: 天祐三年，汴人攻滄、景，劉仁恭遣使求援。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianyou the Bian attacked Cang and Jing; Liu Rengong sent envoys seeking aid.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou 3 the Bian attacked Cang and Jing, and Liu Rengong sent envoys begging for relief.

sentences.zh: 十一月，嗣昭合燕軍三萬進攻潞州，降丁會，武皇乃以嗣昭為昭義節度使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Sizhao joined thirty thousand Yan troops in an attack on Luzhou; Ding Hui surrendered, and the Martial Emperor then appointed Sizhao military commissioner of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Sizhao combined with thirty thousand Yan troops to attack Luzhou. Ding Hui surrendered, and the Martial Emperor appointed Sizhao military commissioner of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 始嗣昭未到之前，上黨有占者，見一人家舍上常有氣如車蓋，視之，但一貧媼而已。

translations.literal: Before Sizhao had yet arrived, at Shangdang a diviner saw above one household's dwelling a vapor like a carriage canopy; looking closer, there was only a poor old woman.
translations.idiomatic: Before Sizhao arrived, a diviner at Shangdang noticed a canopy-like vapor rising above a certain house. He looked closer and found only a poor old woman.

sentences.zh: 占者謂媼：「有子乎？

translations.literal: The diviner asked the old woman, "Do you have a son?"
translations.idiomatic: The diviner asked her, "Do you have a son?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「有，見為軍士，出戍於外。

translations.literal: "She said, "I do; he is presently a soldier on garrison duty abroad."
translations.idiomatic: "She answered, "I do. He is a soldier now, posted on garrison duty elsewhere."

sentences.zh: 」占者心異之，以為其子將來有土地之兆也。

translations.literal: "The diviner was struck inwardly and took it as a sign that her son would one day possess territory.
translations.idiomatic: "The diviner was inwardly astonished and took it as a sign that her son would one day hold territory of his own.

sentences.zh: 未幾，丁會既降，嗣昭領兵入潞，以媼家四面空缺，乃駐於是舍。

translations.literal: Before long, after Ding Hui had surrendered, Sizhao led his troops into Lu and, because the old woman's house was open on all four sides, encamped at that dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, when Ding Hui surrendered, Sizhao entered Lu with his army. The old woman's house stood open on every side, and he made his headquarters there.

sentences.zh: 丁會既歸太原，武皇遣使命嗣昭為帥，乃自媼舍而入理所，其氣尋息，聞者異之。

translations.literal: After Ding Hui had returned to Taiyuan, the Martial Emperor sent orders appointing Sizhao commander; he then entered the administrative quarters from the old woman's dwelling, and the vapor soon ceased—those who heard of it marveled.
translations.idiomatic: After Ding Hui returned to Taiyuan, the Martial Emperor confirmed Sizhao as commander. Sizhao moved from the old woman's house into the official residence, and the strange vapor soon faded. All who heard of it were astonished.

sentences.zh: 四年六月，汴將李思安將兵十萬攻潞州，乃築夾城，深溝高壘，內外重復，飛走路絕。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year the Bian general Li Si'an led one hundred thousand troops to attack Luzhou; he built twin cities, with deep trenches and high ramparts, inner and outer lines repeated, and flying roads and running paths cut off.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourth year the Bian general Li Si'an attacked Luzhou with one hundred thousand men. He built twin siege cities with deep trenches and high walls, inner and outer lines of fortification, and cut off every route in or out.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭撫循士眾，登城拒守，梁祖馳書說誘百端，嗣昭焚其偽詔，斬其使者，城中固守經年，軍民乏絕，感鹽炭自生，以濟貧民。

translations.literal: Sizhao comforted and guided officers and men, mounted the walls and held in defense. The Liang founder sent urgent letters with every sort of persuasion and enticement; Sizhao burned the false edicts and executed the envoys. The city held firm for a year; army and people were exhausted and cut off, yet salt and charcoal appeared as if by miracle to relieve the poor.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao rallied his officers and men and held the walls. The Liang founder sent letter after letter with promises and threats. Sizhao burned the forged edicts and executed the envoys. The city held for a full year while army and people starved, until salt and charcoal appeared as if by miracle to sustain the destitute.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭嘗享諸將，登城張樂，賊矢中足，嗣昭密拔之，坐客不之覺，酣飲如故，以安眾心。

translations.literal: Once when Sizhao feasted the generals, with music played atop the walls, an enemy arrow struck his foot; Sizhao secretly pulled it out without the guests noticing and drank freely as before, to steady the troops' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while feasting his generals with music played on the walls, an enemy arrow struck his foot. Sizhao quietly pulled it out without his guests noticing and drank on as before to steady the men's spirits.

sentences.zh: 五年五月，莊宗敗汴軍，破夾城。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year Emperor Zhuangzong defeated the Bian army and broke the twin cities.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year Zhuangzong defeated the Bian army and broke the siege works.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭知武皇棄世，哀慟幾絕。

translations.literal: When Sizhao learned that the Martial Emperor had passed from the world, he grieved almost to death.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the Martial Emperor had died, Sizhao grieved almost to the point of death.

sentences.zh: 時大兵攻圍曆年，城中士民饑死大半，廛裏蕭條。

translations.literal: The great army had besieged for a year; within the city more than half the soldiers and people died of hunger, and the market districts were desolate.
translations.idiomatic: The great siege had lasted a year. More than half the soldiers and civilians in the city had died of hunger, and the streets lay empty.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭緩法寬租，勸農務穡，一二年間，軍城完集，三面鄰於敵境，寇鈔縱橫，設法枝梧，邊鄙不聳。

translations.literal: Sizhao eased laws and reduced rents, encouraged farming and urged harvest work; within a year or two the garrison city was restored, though on three sides it bordered enemy territory and raiders ranged freely—yet by devising measures to cope, the frontier was not alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao eased the laws, reduced rents, and urged the people back to farming. Within a year or two the garrison city was whole again. Though enemy territory lay on three sides and raiders ranged freely, his measures kept the frontier calm.

sentences.zh: 胡柳之戰，周德威戰沒，師無行列，至晚方集。

translations.literal: At the battle of Huliu, Zhou Dewei fell in battle; the army lost formation and was not gathered until evening.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Huliu, Zhou Dewei was killed in action. The army lost all formation and was not regrouped until evening.

sentences.zh: 汴人四五萬登無石山，我軍懼形於色。

translations.literal: Forty or fifty thousand Bian men climbed Wushi Mountain; fear showed on our troops' faces.
translations.idiomatic: Forty or fifty thousand Bian troops took Wushi Mountain, and fear showed plainly on our men's faces.

sentences.zh: 或請收軍保營，詰旦復戰。

translations.literal: Some urged withdrawing the army to hold the camp and fighting again at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged pulling the army back to camp and renewing the fight at dawn.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭曰：「賊無營壘，去臨濮地遠，日已晡晚，皆有歸心，但以精騎逗撓，無令返旆，晡後追擊，破之必矣。

translations.literal: Sizhao said, "The bandits have no camp or rampart; they are far from Linpu, and the day is already late in the afternoon—they all wish to return. Only use elite cavalry to harass and delay them, do not let them turn their banners back; pursue after the afternoon and you will surely break them."
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao said, "The enemy have no camp. They are far from Linpu, and the afternoon is already late—they all want to get home. Send elite cavalry to harass and delay them. Do not let them turn back. Pursue after dusk and you will break them for certain."

sentences.zh: 我若收軍拔寨，賊人入臨濮，俟彼整齊復來，即勝負水決。

translations.literal: If we withdraw the army and pull up camp, the bandits will enter Linpu; when they regroup and come again, victory and defeat will be decided like tossing a stone into water.
translations.idiomatic: If we pull back and break camp, they will reach Linpu. Once they regroup and return, the outcome will be anyone's guess."

sentences.zh: 」莊宗曰：「非兄言，幾敗吾事！

translations.literal: "Emperor Zhuangzong said, "Had it not been for my brother's words, I would nearly have ruined our cause!"
translations.idiomatic: "Zhuangzong said, "Without your counsel, brother, I would nearly have ruined everything!"

sentences.zh: 」軍校王建及又陳方略，嗣昭與建及分兵於土山南北為掎角，汴軍懼，下山，因縱軍擊之，俘斬三萬級，由是莊宗之軍復振。

translations.literal: "The army officer Wang Jianji also presented a plan; Sizhao and Jianji divided troops north and south of Tushan in pincer formation. The Bian army was afraid, came down the mountain, and our army was unleashed upon them, capturing and slaying thirty thousand; thereby Emperor Zhuangzong's army revived.
translations.idiomatic: "The officer Wang Jianji offered a plan as well. Sizhao and Jianji divided their forces north and south of Tushan in a pincer. The Bian troops, alarmed, came down the mountain, and our army fell upon them, killing and capturing thirty thousand. From that point Zhuangzong's army rallied again.

sentences.zh: 十六年，嗣昭代周德威權幽州軍府事。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Sizhao replaced Zhou Dewei in acting charge of the Youzhou military headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Sizhao took over from Zhou Dewei as acting administrator of the Youzhou military headquarters.

sentences.zh: 九月，以李紹宏代，嗣昭出薊門，百姓號泣請留，截鞍惜別，嗣昭夜遁而歸。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Li Shohong was appointed to replace him; Sizhao went out through Jimen Gate. The people wept and begged him to stay, cutting his saddle in sorrow at parting; Sizhao slipped away by night and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Li Shohong was appointed in his place. As Sizhao left through Jimen Gate, the people wept and begged him to stay, even cutting his saddle straps in their grief at parting. Sizhao stole away by night and returned.

sentences.zh: 十七年六月，嗣昭自德勝歸藩，莊宗帳餞於戚城。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the seventeenth year Sizhao returned to his circuit from Desheng; Emperor Zhuangzong held a farewell feast in his tent at Qicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the seventeenth year Sizhao returned to his circuit from Desheng, and Zhuangzong held a farewell feast for him at Qicheng.

sentences.zh: 莊宗酒酣，泣而言曰：「河朔生靈，十年饋挽，引領鶴望，俟破汴軍。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong was deep in wine, he wept and said, "The people of Hebei have supplied provisions for ten years, stretching their necks like cranes in longing, waiting for the Bian army to be broken."
translations.idiomatic: Deep in his cups, Zhuangzong wept and said, "The people of Hebei have supplied us for ten years, craning their necks in hope, waiting for us to break the Bian army."

sentences.zh: 今兵賦不充，寇孽猶在，坐食軍賦，有愧蒸民。

translations.literal: Now military levies are insufficient, the bandit scourge still remains, and we sit consuming army provisions—we are ashamed before the common people."
translations.idiomatic: Now our levies fall short, the enemy still stands, and we sit here consuming what they provide. I am ashamed before the people."

sentences.zh: 」嗣昭曰：「臣忝急難之地，每一念此，寢不安席。

translations.literal: "Sizhao said, "Your servant holds a post in this land of urgent peril; whenever I think of this, I cannot sleep peacefully on my mat."
translations.idiomatic: "Sizhao said, "I hold a post in this hard-pressed land. Whenever I think of it, I cannot sleep at ease."

sentences.zh: 大王且持重謹守，惠養士民。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should for now hold steady and guard carefully, nurturing officers and people with kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should hold steady, guard carefully, and care for your officers and people.

sentences.zh: 臣歸本藩，簡料兵賦，歲末春首，即舉眾復來。

translations.literal: Your servant will return to his circuit, muster troops and levies, and at year's end or the start of spring will lead the host back again.
translations.idiomatic: I will return to my circuit, gather troops and supplies, and come back with my forces by the end of the year or early spring.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗離席拜送，如家人禮。

translations.literal: "Emperor Zhuangzong left his seat and bowed in farewell, with the courtesy of family.
translations.idiomatic: "Zhuangzong rose from his seat and bowed him off with the intimacy of family.

sentences.zh: 是月，汴將劉鄩攻同州，朱友謙告急，嗣昭與李存審援之。

translations.literal: That month the Bian general Liu Yan attacked Tong Prefecture; Zhu Youqian reported urgently, and Sizhao with Li Cunshen went to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: That same month the Bian general Liu Yan attacked Tong Prefecture. Zhu Youqian sent an urgent appeal, and Sizhao went to his aid with Li Cunshen.

sentences.zh: 九月，破汴軍於馮翊，乃班師。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he defeated the Bian army at Fengyi and then withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he defeated the Bian army at Fengyi and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十九年，莊守親征張文禮於鎮州。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Emperor Zhuang personally campaigned against Zhang Wenli at Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Zhuangzong led a personal campaign against Zhang Wenli at Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 冬，契丹三十萬奄至，嗣昭從莊宗擊之，敵騎圍之數十重，良久不解。

translations.literal: In winter three hundred thousand Khitan suddenly arrived; Sizhao followed Zhuangzong in striking them. Enemy cavalry surrounded them in dozens of rings, and for a long time they could not break free.
translations.idiomatic: That winter three hundred thousand Khitan suddenly appeared. Sizhao followed Zhuangzong into the fight, and enemy cavalry ringed them in layer after layer for a long time without relief.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭號泣赴之，引三百騎橫擊重圍，馳突出沒者數十合，契丹退，翼莊宗而還。

translations.literal: Sizhao wept as he rushed to the rescue, leading three hundred cavalry in a lateral strike through the heavy encirclement, charging in and out dozens of times; the Khitan withdrew, and he shielded Zhuangzong on the return.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao wept as he charged to the rescue with three hundred horsemen, cutting laterally through the encirclement and riding in and out of the enemy ranks dozens of times until the Khitan withdrew. He then escorted Zhuangzong safely back.

sentences.zh: 是時，閻寶為鎮人所敗，退保趙州，莊宗命嗣昭代寶攻真定。

translations.literal: At that time Yan Bao had been defeated by the men of Zhen and withdrew to hold Zhao Prefecture; Emperor Zhuangzong ordered Sizhao to replace Bao in attacking Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yan Bao had been beaten by the men of Zhen and had fallen back to Zhao Prefecture. Zhuangzong ordered Sizhao to replace him and attack Zhending.

sentences.zh: 七月二十四日，王處球之兵出自九門，嗣昭設伏於故營，賊至，發伏，擊之殆盡；

translations.literal: On the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month Wang Chuqin's troops came out through Jiumen Gate; Sizhao set an ambush at the old camp, and when the bandits arrived he sprang the trap and struck them nearly to annihilation;
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fourth of the seventh month Wang Chuqin's troops came out through Jiumen Gate. Sizhao laid an ambush at the old camp, and when the enemy arrived he sprang it and nearly wiped them out;

sentences.zh: 餘三人匿於牆墟間，嗣昭環馬而射之，為賊矢中腦，嗣昭箙中矢盡，拔賊矢於腦射賊，一發而殪之。

translations.literal: three survivors hid among broken walls and ruins; Sizhao circled his horse and shot at them. An enemy arrow struck his brain; the arrows in Sizhao's quiver were exhausted, so he pulled the enemy arrow from his brain and shot the bandit—one shot and the man was killed.
translations.idiomatic: three survivors hid among broken walls. Sizhao circled his horse and shot at them. An enemy arrow struck him in the head. His quiver empty, he pulled the arrow from his own wound and shot one of the survivors dead with a single shot.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭日暮還營，所傷血流不止，是夜卒。

translations.literal: At dusk Sizhao returned to camp; blood from his wound flowed without stopping, and that night he died.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao returned to camp at dusk, but blood from his wound would not stop flowing, and he died that night.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭節制澤、潞，官自司徒、太保至侍中、中書令。

translations.literal: Sizhao governed Ze and Lu; his offices ranged from Grand Preceptor and Grand Guardian to Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao governed Ze and Lu, holding offices from Grand Preceptor and Grand Guardian up to Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 莊宗即位，贈太師、隴西郡王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong took the throne, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor and Prince of Longxi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong took the throne, Sizhao was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor and Prince of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 長興中，詔配饗莊宗廟庭。

translations.literal: In the Changxing era an edict ordered him to share sacrifice in Emperor Zhuangzong's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changxing era an edict ordered that he share offerings in Zhuangzong's ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭有子七人，長曰繼儔，澤州刺史；

translations.literal: Sizhao had seven sons; the eldest was Jichou, prefect of Ze Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao had seven sons. The eldest was Jichou, prefect of Ze;

sentences.zh: 次繼韜、繼忠、繼能、繼襲、繼遠，皆夫人楊氏所生。

translations.literal: next Jitao, Jizhong, Jineng, Jixi, and Jiyuan—all born of Lady Yang.
translations.idiomatic: followed by Jitao, Jizhong, Jineng, Jixi, and Jiyuan, all sons of Lady Yang.

sentences.zh: 楊氏治家善積聚，設法販鬻，致家財百萬。

translations.literal: Lady Yang managed the household well and was skilled at accumulation; she devised methods of trade and sale and amassed family wealth of one million.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang ran the household shrewdly and built up great wealth through trade, amassing a family fortune of one million.

sentences.zh: 繼韜，小字留得，少驕獪無賴。

translations.literal: Jitao, childhood name Liude, was in youth arrogant, cunning, and unruly.
translations.idiomatic: Jitao, known in youth as Liude, was arrogant, cunning, and unruly from an early age.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭既卒，莊宗詔諸子扶喪歸太原襄事，諸子違詔，以父牙兵數千擁喪歸潞。

translations.literal: After Sizhao died, Emperor Zhuangzong ordered the sons to escort the coffin back to Taiyuan for the funeral rites; the sons disobeyed the edict and, with several thousand of their father's guard troops, escorted the coffin back to Lu.
translations.idiomatic: After Sizhao's death Zhuangzong ordered his sons to escort the coffin to Taiyuan for the funeral. They defied the edict and, with several thousand of their father's guard troops, took the coffin back to Lu instead.

sentences.zh: 莊宗令李存渥馳騎追諭，兄弟俱忿，欲害存渥，存渥遁而獲免。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong sent Li Cunwo riding in haste to overtake them and instruct them; the brothers were all enraged and wished to kill Cunwo, who fled and escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong sent Li Cunwo riding after them to deliver his orders. The brothers were furious and meant to kill him, but Cunwo fled and escaped.

sentences.zh: 繼韜兄繼儔，嗣昭長嫡也。

translations.literal: Jitao's elder brother Jichou was Sizhao's eldest legitimate son.
translations.idiomatic: Jitao's elder brother Jichou was Sizhao's eldest legitimate son.

sentences.zh: 當襲父爵，然柔而不武。

translations.literal: He ought to have inherited his father's title, yet he was gentle and not martial.
translations.idiomatic: He should have inherited his father's post, but he was gentle and lacked martial spirit.

sentences.zh: 方在苫廬，繼韜詐令三軍劫己為留後，囚繼儔於別室，以事奏聞。

translations.literal: While still in the mourning hut, Jitao falsely had the three armies seize him as acting military governor, imprisoned Jichou in a separate room, and reported the matter to the court.
translations.idiomatic: While still in mourning, Jitao had the army forcibly proclaim him acting military governor, imprisoned Jichou in a side room, and reported the matter to court.

sentences.zh: 莊宗不得已，命為安義軍兵馬留後。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong had no choice and appointed him acting military governor of the Anyi army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong had no choice but to confirm him as acting military governor of the Anyi army.

sentences.zh: 時軍前糧餉不充，租庸計度請潞州轉米五萬貯於相州；

translations.literal: At that time provisions before the army were insufficient; the rent and corvée accounting office requested that Lu Prefecture transfer fifty thousand piculs of grain to be stored at Xiang Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Provisions at the front were running short, and the revenue office requested that Lu transfer fifty thousand piculs of grain to store at Xiang Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 繼韜辭以經費不足，請轉三萬。

translations.literal: Jitao declined on grounds of insufficient funds and requested transfer of only thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Jitao pleaded insufficient funds and offered only thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 有幕客魏琢、牙將申蒙者，因入奏公事，每摭陰事報繼韜云：「朝廷無人，終為河南吞噬，止遲速間耳。

translations.literal: There were staff member Wei Zhuo and guard officer Shen Meng who, when entering to report official business, would each time gather secret matters and report to Jitao, saying, "The court has no capable men; in the end we will be swallowed by Henan—it is only a matter of sooner or later."
translations.idiomatic: A staff adviser named Wei Zhuo and a guard officer named Shen Meng, whenever they went to court on official business, would gather private intelligence and report to Jitao, "The court has no real leadership. In the end Henan will swallow us—it is only a question of time."

sentences.zh: 」由是陰謀叛計。

translations.literal: "From this they secretly plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: "From this they began to plot rebellion in secret.

sentences.zh: 內官張居翰時為昭義監軍，莊宗將即位，詔赴鄴都。

translations.literal: The inner court official Zhang Juhang was then military supervisor of Zhaoyi; as Emperor Zhuangzong was about to take the throne, an edict ordered him to proceed to Yedu.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Zhang Juhang was then military supervisor of Zhaoyi. As Zhuangzong prepared to take the throne, an edict summoned him to Yedu.

sentences.zh: 潞州節度判官任圜時在鎮州，亦奉詔赴鄴。

translations.literal: Ren Yuan, administrative aide to the military commissioner of Lu, was then at Zhen Prefecture and likewise received an edict to proceed to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yuan, administrative aide to the Lu military commissioner, was then at Zhen Prefecture and received the same summons to Ye.

sentences.zh: 魏琢、申蒙謂繼韜曰：「國家急召此二人，情可知矣。

translations.literal: Wei Zhuo and Shen Meng said to Jitao, "The state has urgently summoned these two men—the situation is plain to see."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhuo and Shen Meng told Jitao, "The court has urgently summoned these two men. You can guess what that means."

sentences.zh: 」弟繼遠，年十五六，謂繼韜曰：「兄有家財百萬，倉儲十年，宜自為謀，莫受人所製。

translations.literal: "His younger brother Jiyuan, fifteen or sixteen years old, said to Jitao, "Elder brother, you have family wealth of one million and stores for ten years—you should plan for yourself and not let others control you."
translations.idiomatic: "His younger brother Jiyuan, only fifteen or sixteen, said to him, "Brother, you have a fortune of a million and stores enough for ten years. Plan for yourself. Do not let others dictate your fate."

sentences.zh: 」繼韜曰：「定哥以為何如？

translations.literal: "Jitao said, "What does Dingge think?"
translations.idiomatic: "Jitao asked, "What do you think, Dingge?"

sentences.zh: 」 曰：「申蒙之言是也。

translations.literal: "He said, "Shen Meng's words are right."
translations.idiomatic: "Jiyuan answered, "Shen Meng is right."

sentences.zh: 河北不勝河南，不如與大梁通盟，國家方事之殷，焉能討我？

translations.literal: Hebei cannot overcome Henan; better to ally with Great Liang. The state is busy with pressing affairs—how can it punish us?
translations.idiomatic: Hebei cannot match Henan. Better to ally with Great Liang. The court is overwhelmed with other business—how could it come after us?

sentences.zh: 無如此算。

translations.literal: There is no plan better than this.
translations.idiomatic: No plan is better than this.

sentences.zh: 」乃令繼遠將百餘騎詐雲於晉、絳擒生，遂至汴。

translations.literal: "He then ordered Jiyuan to lead a little more than one hundred horsemen, falsely claiming they were going to Jin and Jiang to take prisoners, and thus they reached Bian.
translations.idiomatic: "He then sent Jiyuan with a little over one hundred horsemen, pretending they were going to Jin and Jiang to take captives, and so reached Bian.

sentences.zh: 梁主見之喜，因令董璋將兵應接，營於潞州之南，加繼韜同平章事，改昭義軍為匡義軍。

translations.literal: The Liang ruler was pleased to see him and ordered Dong Zhang to lead troops in support, encamping south of Luzhou; Jitao was promoted to Fellow of the Secretariat and the Zhaoyi army was renamed the Kuangyi army.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang ruler received him gladly and sent Dong Zhang with troops to support him, encamping south of Luzhou. Jitao was made Fellow of the Secretariat, and the Zhaoyi army was renamed the Kuangyi army.

sentences.zh: 繼韜令其愛子二人入質於汴。

translations.literal: Jitao sent his two beloved sons as hostages to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Jitao sent his two favorite sons to Bian as hostages.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗平河南，繼韜惶恐，計無所出，將脫身於契丹；

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong pacified Henan, Jitao was terrified and could think of no plan; he was about to escape to the Khitan;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong pacified Henan, Jitao was terrified and at his wits' end. He was about to flee to the Khitan;

sentences.zh: 會有詔赦之，乃齎銀數十萬兩，隨其母楊氏詣闕，冀以賂免。

translations.literal: when an edict arrived pardoning him; he then carried several hundred thousand taels of silver and, with his mother Lady Yang, went to the capital, hoping to buy his freedom with bribes.
translations.idiomatic: when a pardon arrived. He then took several hundred thousand taels of silver and went to the capital with his mother Lady Yang, hoping to buy his way out of trouble.

sentences.zh: 將行，其弟繼遠曰：「兄往與不往，利害一也。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, his younger brother Jiyuan said, "Whether you go or do not go, the advantage and harm are the same."
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared to leave, his brother Jiyuan said, "Whether you go or stay, the outcome is the same."

sentences.zh: 以反為名，何麵更見天下！

translations.literal: Branded as a rebel, what face have you to show the world again!
translations.idiomatic: You are marked as a rebel. What face do you have left to show the world!

sentences.zh: 不如深溝峻壁，坐食積粟，尚可苟延歲月，往則亡無日矣。

translations.literal: Better to dig deep trenches and raise high walls, sit and consume your stored grain—you can still drag out months and years; if you go, destruction will come in no time.
translations.idiomatic: Better to dig in behind deep trenches and high walls and live on your stored grain. You might still buy yourself months or years. If you go to court, you are finished within days.

sentences.zh: 」或曰：「君先世有大功於國，主上季父也，宏農夫人無恙，保獲萬全。

translations.literal: "Someone said, "Your forebears rendered great service to the state; the sovereign is your father's younger brother, and Lady Hongnong is unharmed—you can be assured of complete safety."
translations.idiomatic: "Others said, "Your family served the state with great merit. The emperor is your father's younger brother, and Lady Hongnong is well. You can count on coming through safely."

sentences.zh: 」及繼韜至，厚賂宦官、伶人，言事者翕然稱：「留後本無惡意，奸人惑之故也。

translations.literal: "When Jitao arrived, he lavished bribes on eunuchs and actors; those who spoke on affairs all chimed in, saying, "The acting military governor originally had no evil intent—it was wicked men who misled him."
translations.idiomatic: "When Jitao arrived, he lavished gifts on eunuchs and actors. Court gossips soon agreed: "The acting governor never meant harm. Wicked advisers misled him."

sentences.zh: 嗣昭親賢，不可無嗣。

translations.literal: Sizhao was close and worthy; he cannot be without heirs.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao was a loyal and worthy man. His line must not die out.

sentences.zh: 」楊夫人亦於宮中哀祈劉皇后，後每於莊宗前泣言先人之功，以動聖情，由是原之。

translations.literal: "Lady Yang also pleaded tearfully in the palace to Empress Liu; the empress, weeping before Emperor Zhuangzong each time of her forebear's merits, moved the sovereign's feelings, and thereby he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: "Lady Yang also pleaded tearfully to Empress Liu in the palace. The empress wept before Zhuangzong of her family's old service until he was moved to mercy, and Jitao was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 在京月餘，屢從畋遊，寵待如故。

translations.literal: In the capital for more than a month, he repeatedly joined the hunt, and favor was shown him as before.
translations.idiomatic: He remained in the capital for more than a month, joined the hunt repeatedly, and was treated with favor as before.

sentences.zh: 李存渥深訶詆之，繼韜心不自安，復賂伶閹，求歸本鎮，莊宗不聽。

translations.literal: Li Cunwo harshly reviled and slandered him; Jitao was ill at ease in heart and again bribed actors and eunuchs, seeking to return to his circuit, but Emperor Zhuangzong would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunwo bitterly denounced him. Uneasy in his heart, Jitao bribed actors and eunuchs again to plead for return to his circuit, but Zhuangzong refused.

sentences.zh: 繼韜潛令紀綱書諭繼遠，欲軍城更變，望天子遣己安撫。

translations.literal: Jitao secretly had his guard officers write instructing Jiyuan, wishing the garrison city to rise in mutiny so that the Son of Heaven would dispatch him to pacify it.
translations.idiomatic: Jitao secretly sent word through his guard officers to Jiyuan, hoping to stir mutiny in the garrison so the emperor would send him back to restore order.

sentences.zh: 事泄，斬於天津橋南。

translations.literal: The matter was exposed, and he was beheaded south of Tianjin Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was discovered, and he was beheaded south of Tianjin Bridge.

sentences.zh: 二子齠年質於汴，莊宗收城得之，撫其背曰：「爾幼如是，猶如能佐父造反，長復何為！

translations.literal: His two sons, still in childhood, were hostages at Bian; when Emperor Zhuangzong took the city he obtained them and, patting their backs, said, "You are so young and yet could help your father rebel—what will you do when grown!"
translations.idiomatic: His two young sons had been hostages at Bian. When Zhuangzong took the city he found them and, patting their backs, said, "So young, and already you could help your father rebel. What will you become when you grow up!"

sentences.zh: 」至是亦誅。

translations.literal: "At this time they too were executed.
translations.idiomatic: "They too were executed.

sentences.zh: 乃遣使往潞州斬繼遠，函首赴闕，命繼儔權知軍州事，繼達充軍城巡檢。

translations.literal: He then dispatched envoys to Luzhou to behead Jiyuan and sent the head in a box to the court; he ordered Jichou to act in charge of military and prefectural affairs, and Jida to serve as garrison inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent envoys to Luzhou to behead Jiyuan and deliver the head to court. Jichou was left in charge of military and civil affairs, and Jida was made garrison inspector.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔繼儔赴闕。

translations.literal: Before long an edict ordered Jichou to proceed to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward an edict summoned Jichou to court.

sentences.zh: 時繼儔以繼韜所畜婢仆玩好之類悉為己有，每日料選算校，不時上路。

translations.literal: At that time Jichou took for himself all the maidservants, servants, curios, and fine objects that Jitao had accumulated, reckoning and checking them daily, and did not set out on the road in timely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Jichou seized for himself all the servants, curios, and valuables Jitao had accumulated, inventorying them day after day and delaying his departure.

sentences.zh: 繼達怒謂人曰：「吾仲兄被罪，父子誅死，大兄不仁，略無動懷，而便烝淫妻妾，詰責貨財，慚恥見人，生不如死！

translations.literal: Jida angrily told others, "Our second brother was condemned, father and sons executed to death; the eldest brother is without benevolence, scarcely moved at all, yet at once violates his wives and concubines and presses for goods and wealth—too ashamed to face people; better dead than alive!"
translations.idiomatic: Jida said angrily to others, "Our second brother was condemned and father and sons were killed. Our eldest brother shows no grief at all. Instead he seizes his wives and concubines and haggles over property. I am too ashamed to face anyone. Death would be better than this!"

sentences.zh: 」繼達服縗麻，引數百騎坐於戟門，呼曰：「為我反乎！

translations.literal: "Jida wore mourning hemp, led several hundred horsemen to sit at the halberd gate, and shouted, "Will you rebel for me!"
translations.idiomatic: "Jida put on mourning dress, led several hundred horsemen to the halberd gate, and shouted, "Will you rebel for me!"

sentences.zh: 」即令人斬繼儔首，投於戟門之內。

translations.literal: "He then had someone behead Jichou and cast the head inside the halberd gate.
translations.idiomatic: "He then had Jichou beheaded and the head thrown inside the halberd gate.

sentences.zh: 副使李繼珂聞其亂也，募市人千餘攻於城門。

translations.literal: Deputy commissioner Li Jike, hearing of the disorder, recruited more than a thousand townspeople to attack at the city gate.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commissioner Li Jike, hearing of the turmoil, recruited more than a thousand townspeople to attack the gate.

sentences.zh: 繼達登城樓，知事不濟，啟子城東門，至其第，盡殺其孥，得百餘騎，出潞城門，將奔契丹。

translations.literal: Jida mounted the city tower, knew the affair would not succeed, opened the east gate of the inner city, went to his residence, killed all his dependents, gathered a little more than one hundred horsemen, went out through Lu city gate, and was about to flee to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Jida mounted the tower, saw that the affair was lost, opened the inner city's east gate, went to his house and killed his entire household, gathered a little over one hundred horsemen, left through the Lu city gate, and fled toward the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 行不十里，麾下奔潰，自剄於路隅。

translations.literal: Having gone less than ten li, his followers scattered in flight; he cut his own throat at the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten li his followers scattered. He cut his own throat by the roadside.

sentences.zh: 天成初，繼能為相州刺史，母楊氏卒於太原，繼能、繼襲奔喪行服。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng, Jineng was prefect of Xiang; Lady Yang died at Taiyuan, and Jineng and Jixi hurried home for mourning and wore mourning garb.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tiancheng era Jineng was prefect of Xiang. When Lady Yang died at Taiyuan, Jineng and Jixi returned home to mourn.

sentences.zh: 繼能笞掠母主藏婢，責金銀數，因笞至死。

translations.literal: Jineng flogged and plundered his mother's chief storehouse maid, demanding a count of gold and silver, and flogged her to death.
translations.idiomatic: Jineng beat and robbed his mother's chief storekeeper, demanding an accounting of gold and silver, and flogged her to death.

sentences.zh: 家人告變，言聚甲為亂，繼能、繼襲皆伏誅。

translations.literal: The household reported the disturbance, saying they were gathering armor to rebel; Jineng and Jixi were both executed.
translations.idiomatic: The household reported them for gathering arms to rebel. Jineng and Jixi were both executed.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭諸子自相屠害，幾於溘盡，惟繼忠一人僅保其首領焉。

translations.literal: Sizhao's sons slaughtered one another and were nearly all extinguished; only Jizhong alone barely preserved his life.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao's sons destroyed one another until nearly none remained. Only Jizhong barely kept his life.

sentences.zh: 裴約，潞州之舊將也。

translations.literal: Pei Yue was an old officer of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yue was a veteran officer of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 初事李嗣昭為親信，及繼韜之叛，約方戍澤州，因召民泣而諭之曰：「餘事故使，已餘二紀，每見分財享士，志在平讎，不幸薨歿。

translations.literal: He had first served Li Sizhao as a trusted man; when Jitao rebelled, Yue was then garrisoning Ze Prefecture. He summoned the people and, weeping, instructed them, saying, "I have served the late commissioner for more than twenty years; I always saw him distribute wealth and feast officers, his aim to settle scores—unfortunately he passed away."
translations.idiomatic: He had long served Li Sizhao as a trusted officer. When Jitao rebelled, Yue was garrisoning Ze Prefecture. He summoned the people and, weeping, told them, "I served the late commissioner for more than twenty years. I always saw him share his wealth with his men and strive to settle old scores. Now he is gone."

sentences.zh: 今郎君父喪未葬，即背君親，餘可倳刃自殺，不能送死與人。

translations.literal: Now the young master, his father's funeral not yet buried, turns against lord and kin—I can turn the blade on myself, but I cannot hand over the dead to others."
translations.idiomatic: Now the young master rebels before his father's funeral is even complete. I would rather turn the blade on myself than betray my dead lord to another."

sentences.zh: 」眾皆感泣。

translations.literal: "All were moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: "All wept with emotion.

sentences.zh: 繼而梁以董璋為澤州刺史，率眾攻城，約拒久之，告急於莊宗。

translations.literal: Presently Liang appointed Dong Zhang prefect of Ze and led the host to assault the city; Yue resisted for a long time and reported urgently to Emperor Zhuangzong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Liang appointed Dong Zhang prefect of Ze and besieged the city. Yue held out for a long time and sent an urgent appeal to Zhuangzong.

sentences.zh: 莊宗知其忠懇，謂諸將曰：「朕於繼韜何薄，於裴約何厚？

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong knew his loyalty and earnestness and said to the generals, "What have I done lightly by Jitao, or heavily by Pei Yue?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong knew his loyalty and said to his generals, "What have I done for Jitao, and what have I done for Pei Yue?"

sentences.zh: 裴約能分逆順，不附賊黨，先兄一何不幸，生此鴟梟！

translations.literal: Pei Yue can distinguish rebellion from loyalty and will not attach himself to the bandit faction—how unfortunate my elder brother was to have borne this owl and kite!"
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yue knows right from rebellion and will not join the traitors. How unlucky my elder brother was to have fathered such vultures!"

sentences.zh: 」乃顧李紹斌曰：「爾識機便，為我取裴約來，朕不藉澤州彈丸之地。

translations.literal: "He then turned to Li Shaobin and said, "You understand opportune moments—bring Pei Yue to me. I do not rely on Ze Prefecture, a pellet of land."
translations.idiomatic: "He then turned to Li Shaobin and said, "You know how to move quickly. Bring Pei Yue to me. I do not need a place as small as Ze Prefecture."

sentences.zh: 」即遣紹斌率五千騎以赴之。

translations.literal: "He immediately dispatched Shaobin leading five thousand cavalry to go to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: "He immediately sent Shaobin with five thousand cavalry to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 紹斌自遼州進軍，未至，城已陷，約被害，時同光元年六月也。

translations.literal: Shaobin advanced from Liaozhou; before he arrived the city had fallen and Yue was killed—it was the sixth month of the first year of Tongguang.
translations.idiomatic: Shaobin marched from Liaozhou, but before he arrived the city had fallen and Yue was killed. This was the sixth month of Tongguang 1.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，嗟痛不已。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he sighed in grief without end.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard the news, he mourned without end.

sentences.zh: 李嗣本，雁門人，本姓張。

translations.literal: Li Siben was a man of Yanmen, originally surnamed Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siben was from Yanmen and was originally surnamed Zhang.

sentences.zh: 父準，銅冶鎮將。

translations.literal: His father Zhun was commander of Tongye Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhun was commander of Tongye Garrison.

sentences.zh: 嗣本少事武皇，為帳中紀綱，漸立戰功，得補軍校。

translations.literal: Siben in youth served the Martial Emperor as a guard officer in the tent, gradually achieved merit in battle, and was appointed a military cadet.
translations.idiomatic: Siben served the Martial Emperor from youth as a guard officer in his tent, gradually won distinction in battle, and was appointed a military cadet.

sentences.zh: 乾寧中，從征李匡儔為前鋒，與燕人戰，得居庸關，以功為義兒軍使，因賜姓名。

translations.literal: During Qianning he followed the campaign against Li Kuangchou as vanguard, fought the Yan men, took Juyong Pass, and for his merit was made commander of the adoptive-sons army; he was thereupon granted the surname and given name.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianning era he served as vanguard in the campaign against Li Kuangchou, fought the Yan forces, and took Juyong Pass. For this he was made commander of the adoptive-sons army and granted the Li surname and his given name.

sentences.zh: 從討王行瑜，授檢校刑部尚書，改威遠、寧塞等軍使。

translations.literal: He followed the punitive campaign against Wang Xingyu and was appointed acting Minister of Justice, then changed to commander of the Weiyuan, Ningsai, and other armies.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Wang Xingyu and was appointed acting Minister of Justice, then made commander of the Weiyuan, Ningsai, and other armies.

sentences.zh: 五年，討羅宏信於魏州，嗣本為前鋒，師還，改馬軍都將。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he campaigned against Luo Hongxin at Weizhou; Siben was vanguard. When the army returned he was changed to commander of the horse army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he campaigned against Luo Hongxin at Weizhou as vanguard. When the army returned he was made commander of the horse army.

sentences.zh: 從李嗣昭討王暉於雲州，論功加檢校司空。

translations.literal: He followed Li Sizhao in campaigning against Wang Hui at Yun Prefecture; for merit he was promoted to acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Li Sizhao against Wang Hui at Yun Prefecture and was promoted to acting Minister of Works for his service.

sentences.zh: 汴將李思安之圍潞州也，從周德威軍於餘吾，嗣本率騎軍日與汴人轉鬥，前後獻俘千計，遷代州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Bian general Li Si'an besieged Luzhou, he followed Zhou Dewei's army at Yuyu; Siben led cavalry daily in running battles with the Bian, presenting more than a thousand captives in all, and was transferred to military commissioner of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: When the Bian general Li Si'an besieged Luzhou, he served under Zhou Dewei at Yuyu. Siben led cavalry in daily skirmishes with the Bian, presented more than a thousand captives in all, and was made military commissioner of Dai.

sentences.zh: 六年，從攻晉、絳，為蕃漢副使都校。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed the attack on Jin and Jiang and was deputy commander of the mixed Tangut-Han forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he joined the attack on Jin and Jiang as deputy commander of the mixed Tangut-Han forces.

sentences.zh: 及武皇喪事有日，嗣本監護其事，改雲中防禦使、雲蔚應朔等州都知兵馬使，加特進、檢校太保。

translations.literal: When the Martial Emperor's funeral was near, Siben supervised the arrangements; he was changed to defender of Yunzhong and overall commander of troops for Yun, Wei, Ying, Shuo, and other prefectures, with special advancement and acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When the Martial Emperor's funeral drew near, Siben supervised the arrangements. He was made defender of Yunzhong and overall commander of troops for Yun, Wei, Ying, Shuo, and other prefectures, with special advancement and the acting rank of Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 九年，周德威討劉守光，嗣本率代北諸軍、生熟吐渾，收山後八軍，得納降軍使盧文進、武州刺史高行珪以獻。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Zhou Dewei campaigned against Liu Shouguang; Siben led the armies of northern Dai and raw and seasoned Tuyuhun, recovered the eight armies beyond the mountains, and presented the surrendered commander Lu Wenjin and the prefect of Wu Gao Xinggui.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Zhou Dewei campaigned against Liu Shouguang. Siben led the northern Dai armies and Tuyuhun forces, recovered the eight armies beyond the mountains, and presented the surrendered commander Lu Wenjin and Wu prefect Gao Xinggui.

sentences.zh: 幽州平，論功授振武節度使，號「威信可汗」。

translations.literal: When Youzhou was pacified, for merit he was appointed military commissioner of Zhenwu and styled "Trustworthy and Worthy Khan."
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhou was pacified, he was rewarded with the post of military commissioner of Zhenwu and styled "Trustworthy and Worthy Khan."

sentences.zh: 十二年，莊宗定魏博，劉鄩據莘縣，命嗣本入太原巡守都城，十三年，從破劉鄩於故元城，收洺、磁、衛三郡。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Emperor Zhuangzong secured Weibo; Liu Yan held Shen County, and Siben was ordered into Taiyuan to patrol and guard the capital. In the thirteenth year he followed the defeat of Liu Yan at Old Yuancheng and recovered the three commanderies of Mo, Ci, and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Zhuangzong secured Weibo while Liu Yan held Shen County. Siben was ordered into Taiyuan to guard the capital. In the thirteenth year he helped defeat Liu Yan at Old Yuancheng and recovered Mo, Ci, and Wei.

sentences.zh: 六月，還鎮振武。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he returned to his post at Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he returned to his post at Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 八月，契丹阿保機傾塞犯邊，其眾三十萬攻振武，嗣本嬰城拒戰者累日。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Khitan Abaoji poured across the frontier in invasion; his host of three hundred thousand attacked Zhenwu, and Siben held the city and resisted in battle for many days.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Khitan ruler Abaoji invaded in force with three hundred thousand men against Zhenwu. Siben held the city and fought for many days.

sentences.zh: 契丹為火車地道，晝夜急攻，城中兵少，禦備罄竭，城陷，嗣本舉族入契丹。

translations.literal: The Khitan used fire carts and tunneling, attacking urgently day and night; troops in the city were few, defenses exhausted, the city fell, and Siben led his whole clan into Khitan territory.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan used fire carts and tunneling and attacked day and night without pause. The garrison was small, defenses were exhausted, the city fell, and Siben took his whole clan into Khitan territory.

sentences.zh: 有子八人，四人陷於幕庭。

translations.literal: He had eight sons; four were lost in the Khitan court.
translations.idiomatic: He had eight sons, four of whom were lost in the Khitan court.

sentences.zh: 嗣本性剛烈，有節義，善戰多謀，然治郡民，頗傷苛急，人以此少之也。

translations.literal: Siben by nature was stern and fierce, possessed integrity and righteousness, was skilled in battle and full of stratagems; yet in governing prefectural people he was rather harsh and severe, and for this people thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: Siben was stern and principled, skilled in battle and full of stratagems. Yet in governing his prefecture he was harsh, and for that people thought less of him.

sentences.zh: 李嗣恩，本姓駱。

translations.literal: Li Si'en was originally surnamed Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Li Si'en was originally surnamed Luo.

sentences.zh: （《歐陽史》：嗣恩本吐谷渾部人。）〉

translations.literal: (The Ouyang History: Si'en was originally a man of the Tuyuhun tribe.)]
translations.idiomatic: (The Ouyang History records that Si'en was originally from the Tuyuhun people.)]

sentences.zh: 年十五，能騎射，侍武皇於振武；

translations.literal: At fifteen he could ride and shoot and attended the Martial Emperor at Zhenwu;
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he could ride and shoot and attended the Martial Emperor at Zhenwu;

sentences.zh: 及鎮太原，補鐵林軍小校。

translations.literal: when the emperor took up his post at Taiyuan, he was appointed a junior officer of the Iron Forest Army.
translations.idiomatic: when the emperor took charge at Taiyuan, he was appointed a junior officer in the Iron Forest Army.

sentences.zh: 從征王行瑜，奉表獻捷，加檢校散騎常侍，漸轉突陣指揮使，賜姓名。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Wang Xingyu, presented a memorial reporting victory, was promoted to acting Regular Attendant, gradually became commander of the shock-assault formation, and was granted the surname and given name.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Wang Xingyu, reported victory to court, was promoted to acting Regular Attendant, became commander of the shock-assault formation, and was granted the Li surname and his given name.

sentences.zh: 天祐四年，逐康懷英於河西，解汾州之圍，加檢校司空，充左廂馬軍都將。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianyou he drove Kang Huaiying from Hexi, relieved the siege of Fen Prefecture, was promoted to acting Minister of Works, and served as commander of the left wing of the horse army.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou 4 he drove Kang Huaiying from Hexi, lifted the siege of Fen Prefecture, was promoted to acting Minister of Works, and made commander of the left wing of the horse army.

sentences.zh: 戰王景仁有功，加檢校司徒。

translations.literal: Fighting Wang Jingren he achieved merit and was promoted to acting Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Wang Jingren with distinction and was promoted to acting Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 救河中府，與梁人接戰，應弦斃者甚眾，而槊中其口；

translations.literal: Relieving Hezhong Prefecture, he engaged the Liang in battle; many fell to his arrows, but a spear struck his mouth;
translations.idiomatic: Relieving Hezhong, he fought the Liang in battle. Many fell to his arrows, but a spear struck him in the mouth;

sentences.zh: 及退，莊宗親視其傷，深加慰勉，轉內衙馬步都將、遼州刺史。

translations.literal: when he withdrew, Emperor Zhuangzong personally inspected his wound and greatly comforted and encouraged him; he was transferred to commander of the inner guard horse and foot forces and prefect of Liao.
translations.idiomatic: when he withdrew Zhuangzong personally inspected his wound and comforted him warmly. He was made commander of the inner guard horse and foot forces and prefect of Liao.

sentences.zh: 十二年，從莊宗入魏，擊劉鄩有功，轉天雄軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he followed Emperor Zhuangzong into Wei, struck Liu Yan with merit, and was transferred to overall commander of the Tianxiong army.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he followed Zhuangzong into Wei, fought Liu Yan with distinction, and was made overall commander of the Tianxiong army.

sentences.zh: 劉鄩之北趣樂平也，嗣恩襲之，倍程先入晉陽。

translations.literal: When Liu Yan marched north toward Leping, Si'en struck him, doubled the pace, and entered Jinyang first.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yan marched north toward Leping, Si'en struck at him, forced the pace, and entered Jinyang ahead of him.

sentences.zh: 時城中無備，得嗣恩兵至，人百其勇，鄩聞其先過，乃遁。

translations.literal: At that time the city had no preparations; when Si'en's troops arrived, each man was a hundred times braver; Yan, hearing he had passed ahead, then fled.
translations.idiomatic: The city was unprepared. When Si'en's troops arrived, every man fought as if he were worth a hundred. Yan, hearing that Si'en had passed him, fled.

sentences.zh: 莘之戰，以功轉代州刺史，充石嶺關以北都知兵馬使，稍遷振武節度使。

translations.literal: At the battle of Shen, for merit he was transferred to military commissioner of Dai, served as overall commander of troops north of Shiling Pass, and was gradually promoted to military commissioner of Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Shen he was rewarded with the post of military commissioner of Dai and overall commander of troops north of Shiling Pass, and was later promoted to military commissioner of Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 十五年，追赴行在，卒於太原。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was summoned in haste to the imperial camp and died at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was summoned urgently to the imperial camp and died at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 天成初，明宗敦念舊勳，詔贈太尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng, Emperor Ming deeply recalled old merit and issued an edict posthumously enfeoffing him as Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tiancheng era Emperor Ming, mindful of old service, posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 有子二人，長曰武八，騎射推於軍中。

translations.literal: He had two sons; the eldest was called Wuba, renowned in the army for riding and shooting.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons. The eldest was called Wuba and was renowned in the army for riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 嘗有時輩臂饑鷹，矜其搏擊，武八持鳴鏑一隻，賭其狩獲，暮乃多之。

translations.literal: Once men of the time carried hungry hawks on their arms and boasted of their striking power; Wuba held a single whistling arrow and wagered on their hunting catch—by evening he had more.
translations.idiomatic: Once some companions carried hungry hawks on their arms and boasted of their hunting prowess. Wuba wagered with a single whistling arrow on the day's catch, and by evening he had taken more game.

sentences.zh: 戰契丹於親州，歿焉。

translations.literal: Fighting the Khitan at Qin Prefecture, he perished there.
translations.idiomatic: He died fighting the Khitan at Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼曰從郎，累為行軍司馬。

translations.literal: The younger was called Conglang and repeatedly served as campaign marshal.
translations.idiomatic: The younger son was called Conglang and served repeatedly as campaign marshal.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：嗣昭以精悍勤勞，佐經綸之業，終沒王事，得以為忠，然其後嗣皆不免於刑戮者，何也？

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Sizhao, through keenness, diligence, and toil, assisted in the work of statecraft and in the end died in the king's service, thereby achieving loyalty—yet why were his descendants none of them spared execution?
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Sizhao, through keen ability and tireless labor, helped build the state and died in its service, earning the name of loyalty. Yet why did his descendants all end on the execution ground?

sentences.zh: 蓋貨殖無窮，多財累愚故也。

translations.literal: Surely it was because boundless accumulation of wealth and great riches burdened the foolish.
translations.idiomatic: Surely it was because boundless wealth and great riches made fools of them.

sentences.zh: 抑苟能以清白遺子孫，安有斯禍哉！

translations.literal: Yet if one could leave purity and integrity to one's descendants, how could there be such calamity!
translations.idiomatic: Had he been able to leave his descendants integrity rather than riches, how could such calamity have followed!

sentences.zh: 裴約以偏裨而效忠烈，尤可貴也。

translations.literal: Pei Yue, a mere subordinate officer, displayed loyal valor—this is especially worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yue, though only a subordinate officer, showed loyal valor, and that is especially admirable.

sentences.zh: 嗣本、嗣恩皆以中涓之效，參再造之功，故可附於茲也。

translations.literal: Siben and Si'en both, through service as inner attendants, shared in the achievement of restoration—therefore they may be appended here.
translations.idiomatic: Siben and Si'en both served as inner attendants and shared in the work of restoration, and so they are recorded here as well.
